page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance configuration featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The hardware architecture utilizes the x86_64 instruction set, offering 35 MB of L3 cache, along with support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions. Memory capacity measures 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Physical storage includes 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not bundle hardware GPUs.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate balanced multi-threaded throughput contrasted with modest single-thread efficiency. The instance achieved 54132.74 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 44078.3, both falling within the middle range of measured systems. Extended instruction workloads showed higher relative efficiency, registering 52991.8 on PassMark. Conversely, single-thread evaluations yielded lower results, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1055.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 1284.68, placing them in the lower quartile. Memory throughput remained steady, highlighted by 189.99 GB/sec in large-block uncached read bandwidth.

Resource allocation provides solid cost efficiency for aggregated multi-core demands and large in-memory footprints requiring direct high-speed local disk storage. The primary tradeoff stems from its older microarchitecture, which limits performance in latency-critical, single-threaded processing and CPU-bound text token generation. Workloads best aligned with the m5d.16xlarge include relational and NoSQL database clusters, distributed caching tiers such as Redis, batch data processing, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice backends requiring fast local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance powered by a 32-core, 64-thread Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. It integrates 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 2400 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage, and a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations illustrate dependable multi-core and memory capabilities, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 44078.3 and 189.99 GB/sec in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth, while single-core performance remains modest across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. The balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio paired with fast local disk makes this configuration cost-efficient for aggregated multi-threaded environments. It is well suited for database deployments, distributed caching systems, software build clusters, and data-intensive batch processing pipelines.
